consumer.use: Decide whether a bounded Chronik history brief should remain opt-in, be preferred for explicit coding task classes, or be rejected.

decision_target.question: Does a frozen repo- and component-specific Chronik history brief reduce avoidable repeated coding errors without causing stale-history or false-confidence regressions?

intervention.name: pre-decision Chronik history brief
intervention.description: Before planning, provide a hash-bound historical-only Chronik cohort selected by repo, component and operation; all ordinary live preflight checks remain unchanged.

control_condition.description: Use the ordinary Grabowski live-first preflight without a Chronik history brief.

treatment_condition.description: Use the same live-first preflight plus one frozen Chronik history brief before planning and record whether it changes the decision.

measurement.method: An independent blinded reviewer scores each completed case from immutable execution, review and outcome evidence using the registered additive binary scorecard.
measurement.success: The conservative 95 percent interval is above one point with no fatal history-as-live-truth failure and proportionate effort.
measurement.falsification: Any fatal history-as-live-truth failure, materially worse score, or repeated false-confidence regression falsifies promotion.

components.criterion: The work does not unnecessarily repeat a previously evidenced failed path.
The target repository, component and operation are identified correctly.
Every historical statement used for action is checked against current live state.
The final outcome is bound to concrete execution, GitHub, CI or runtime evidence.
Chronik history is never treated as current Git, CI, runtime or safe-retry truth.

cost_metric.method: Measure elapsed operator handling time from live-preflight start until the initial implementation decision is sealed.

comparison.unit: natural coding task in the same registered task-class, risk and context band

allowed: GitHub pull request and CI evidence
